title: Prueba de optimalidad por cota de disponibilidad de elementos grandes
text:
Para que una mediana m_i sea mediana, necesita un elemento estrictamente mayor que no se reutilice en otros triples. Se obtiene que para las medianas ordenadas, debe cumplirse una desigualdad que fuerza m_{n-k+1} ≤ 3n - 2k + 1, que coincide con la construcción óptima.

“Each median needs an element strictly larger than it not used in any other triple. So there should be at least 1 element larger than m_n, at least 3 elements larger than m_{n-1} ... and more generally, at least 2k - 1 elements larger than m_{n-k+1}.” y “we need 2k-1 ≤ 3n - m_{n-k+1} ... Rearranging, we get m_{n-k+1} ≤ 3n - 2k + 1, as in the optimal construction.”

title: Construcción 1: b_i como primos consecutivos
text:
Elegir b_i como los primos 2,3,5,... (n+1 primos distintos) y definir a_i=b_i*b_{i+1}. Como todos los b son coprimos entre sí, gcd(b_i,b_{i+2})=1 y la construcción es válida.

“One way to obtain this is to let all b_i be all primes starting from 2,3,5,... . Since all numbers are coprime to each other, their pairwise gcd is 1 and we get a valid construction.”

title: Modelo matemático: maximizar x ⊕ y
text:
Como el resultado final es x ⊕ y, el problema se reduce a encontrar el máximo a_x ⊕ a_y sobre todos los pares (x, y) posibles.

“Since n is small, it is enough to brute force all possible pairs (x, y). The answer is the maximum value of a_x ⊕ a_y among all pairs.”

title: Construcción 2: b_i como impares y usar gcd(x,x+4)=1
text:
Elegir b_i como impares 1,3,5,... (n+1 impares). La editorial indica que gcd(x,x+4)=1 para x impar, lo que hace válida la condición necesaria para i separados por 2.

“Another way to obtain this to let all b_i be odd numbers starting from 1,3,5,... . Since gcd(x,x+4)=1, where x is odd, this construction is also valid.”

title: Justificación (esbozo) del invariante
text:
El editorial muestra explícitamente los casos de 1 y 2 operaciones y luego generaliza: tras 2 operaciones el elemento de la primera elección no afecta; tras 3 tampoco afectan las dos primeras; por inducción solo importan el último elegido y el nunca elegido, dando x ⊕ y.

“After the second operation... independent of a_1... when doing three operations... Inductively... The final value... x ⊕ y.”

title: Brute force de pares para maximizar XOR
text:
Enumerar todos los pares (x, y) y calcular a_x ⊕ a_y; devolver el máximo.

“it is enough to brute force all possible pairs (x, y). The answer is the maximum value of a_x ⊕ a_y among all pairs.”

title: Contar opciones de a_i y multiplicar
text:
Iterar sobre cada persona i, hallar el tiempo más temprano en que se sentó alguno de sus vecinos para decidir Tipo A o Tipo B, calcular cuántos valores posibles de a_i hay según c_t, y multiplicar todas las cantidades módulo 676767677.

“We can iterate over all people i and look at the earliest time one of their neighbours sat down to find out which type of person they are, and then compute how many valid a_i there are for them. Finally, we can multiply the number of valid a_i for every person, and output this modulo 676767677.”

title: Relación clave de gcd
text:
Se obtiene gcd(a_i,a_{i+1}) = b_{i+1} * gcd(b_i, b_{i+2}). Si gcd(b_i,b_{i+2})=1 para todo i, entonces los gcd adyacentes quedan determinados por b_{i+1} y son distintos.

“Now gcd(a_i,a_{i+1})=b_{i+1}·gcd(b_i,b_{i+2}). Now if gcd(b_i,b_{i+2})=1 for all i, then we can obtain a distinct gcd for each adjacent pair and the construction is valid.”

title: Tipo A: condición 1 primero
text:
Tipo A: la persona está esperando a que un vecino se siente. Es de Tipo A si el tiempo más temprano en que se sienta alguno de sus vecinos es exactamente 1 menos que su tiempo de asiento. Entonces a_i puede ser cualquier valor entre 1 y c_{t-1} inclusive: c_{t-1} posibilidades.

“Type A: Condition 1 is satisfied first... A person is of this type if the earliest time one of their neighbours sat down is exactly 1 less than the time they sat down. This means their a_i can be any value between 1 and c_{t-1} inclusive so there are c_{t-1} possible values.”

title: Paso clave: contar elementos mayores necesarios
text:
Si las medianas están ordenadas, para m_{n-k+1} se requieren al menos 2k-1 elementos estrictamente mayores (por m_n, r_n, r_{n-1}, etc.).

“at least 1 element larger than m_n, at least 3 elements larger than m_{n-1} (namely m_n, r_n, r_{n-1}), and more generally, at least 2k - 1 elements larger than m_{n-k+1}.”

title: Tipo B: condición 2 primero
text:
Tipo B: la persona está esperando a que haya suficientes personas sentadas. Es de Tipo B si el tiempo de asiento es al menos 2 mayor que el tiempo más temprano de sus vecinos. Como no se sentó en t-1, su a_i debe ser mayor que c_{t-2}; por tanto a_i está entre c_{t-2}+1 y c_{t-1} inclusive, dando c_{t-1}-c_{t-2} posibilidades.

“Type B: Condition 2 is satisfied first... A person is of this type if the time they sit down is at least 2 greater than the earliest time one of their neighbours sat down. Since they did not sit down at time t-1, their a_i must be greater than c_{t-2}. This means it must be between c_{t-2}+1 and c_{t-1} inclusive, giving c_{t-1}-c_{t-2} possibilities.”

title: Paso clave: desigualdad y reordenamiento
text:
En {1..3n}, hay exactamente 3n - m_{n-k+1} elementos mayores que m_{n-k+1}. Entonces 2k-1 ≤ 3n - m_{n-k+1} y se reordena a m_{n-k+1} ≤ 3n - 2k + 1.

“In the set 1 ... 3n, there are 3n - m_{n-k+1} elements larger than m_{n-k+1} ... and so we need 2k-1 ≤ 3n - m_{n-k+1}. Rearranging, we get m_{n-k+1} ≤ 3n - 2k + 1”

title: Even-subtree vertex must have an odd-sized child
text:
If a vertex has even subtree size, it must have at least one child whose subtree size is odd; otherwise the subtree size would be odd (sum of evens plus the node).

“for any vertex whose subtree has an even size, it must have at least one child with an odd size. Indeed, suppose all of its children have even size. Then ... the sum of some even numbers, plus one, the node itself.”

title: If even-count exceeds odd-count (excluding root), answer is NO
text:
Using the observation, each even-subtree vertex (excluding root) needs at least one odd-subtree child, so if the number of even-subtree vertices is larger than the number of odd-subtree vertices (excluding the root), no valid tree exists.

“Therefore, if the number of vertices with an even subtree size is larger than the number of vertices with an odd subtree size (excluding the root), there is no valid tree.”

title: Construct using x disjoint pairs attached to root
text:
Make every vertex (excluding the root) have subtree size either 1 or 2 by attaching x disjoint pairs of vertices; then attach each pair and all remaining vertices to the root. The number of vertices with even subtree size becomes exactly x (the parent from each pair).

“we will try to make every vertex (excluding the root) have subtree size either 1 or 2. ... attach x disjoint pairs of vertices. Then we will attach each pair, and all of the remaining vertices, to the root. Now, the number of vertices with an even subtree size is exactly x, the parent from each of the pairs”
